header.title: Transition
header.description: Animates its content in and out. Control presence with `in` and pick the motion with `effect`: fade, scale, four slides and collapse. By default the content unmounts once it finishes exiting.

playground.title: Playground
playground.description: Adjust the props and use the button to see the enter and exit.

base.title: Basic usage
base.description: Wrap the content and change `in` to show or hide it. With no other props it uses a 220 ms `fade`. The first time it mounts with `in` set to `true`, it appears without animation.

effects.title: Effects
effects.description: `effect` accepts `fade`, `scale`, `slide-up`, `slide-down`, `slide-left`, `slide-right` and `collapse`. Slides combine movement and opacity; `collapse` animates the height.

collapse.title: Show and hide content
collapse.description: For a disclosure, use `collapse` with a button that has `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. Pass `unmountOnExit={false}` so the `id` that `aria-controls` points to always exists.

texts.title: Advanced options
texts.body: These options change how the report is exported. You rarely need to touch them.

timing.title: Duration, delay and easing
timing.description: `duration` takes milliseconds, or `{ enter, exit }` for split timing. `delay` applies to both enter and exit, and `easing` accepts any CSS curve.

stagger.title: Staggered entrance
stagger.description: With a different `delay` per element, items appear one by one. On exit the order is reversed. `Transition` goes inside each `<li>` so the list structure stays intact.

appear.title: Animate on mount
appear.description: With `appear`, the first mount also animates even when already visible. Useful for content that arrives after loading.

keepMounted.title: Keep mounted
keepMounted.description: By default, content unmounts on exit and loses its state. With `unmountOnExit={false}` it stays in the DOM, transparent and inert, and keeps taking up space. Type in both fields, hide them and show them again.

renderProp.title: Transition status
renderProp.description: `children` can be a function that receives the status: `entering`, `entered`, `exiting` or `exited`. Use it to adapt the content to each phase.

callbacks.title: Events
callbacks.description: `onEnter`, `onEntering` and `onEntered` report each enter phase; `onExit`, `onExiting` and `onExited`, the exit ones. `onExited` runs before unmounting.

header.title: Transition API
header.description: API reference for the React Transition: props, events, CSS classes, variables and exported types.

demos.title: Demos
demos.description: For examples and usage details, visit the component demo page.

import.title: Import
import.description: Import it from the main entry or from its subpath.

inheritance.title: Inheritance
inheritance.body: Transition accepts <div> attributes. They go to the container it adds around the content. children also accepts a function that receives the status.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.reducedMotion: It respects prefers-reduced-motion: with that preference, it enters and exits instantly.
a11y.hidden: When it exits and stays mounted, it gets hidden, inert and aria-hidden: it can't be focused and screen readers skip it. Because the component class sets display, hidden doesn't remove it from the layout: it keeps taking up space, transparent.
a11y.focus: It doesn't move focus. If focus was inside the content that exits, it's lost: return it to the button that hid it.
a11y.disclosure: To show and hide content, use a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls. aria-controls needs unmountOnExit={false} so the element always exists.
a11y.announce: Appearing content isn't announced. If it's an important notice, put it in an aria-live region or use a component that has one, like Toast.
a11y.wrapper: It adds a <div> around the content. Inside lists or tables, place it inside each <li> or cell so the structure stays valid.
a11y.duration: Keep animations short and don't use motion as the only way to communicate something.

cssClasses.title: CSS classes
cssClasses.description: Classes you can use to override styles. Only one phase class is applied at a time.

rules.root: Container. Receives `className` and `classNames.root`. It's `inline-block` by default.
rules.enter: First enter frame, with the initial state.
rules.enterActive: Enter in progress. Holds the CSS `transition`.
rules.exitActive: Exit in progress. Holds the CSS `transition`.
rules.exited: Hidden: transparent with no pointer events. If it stays mounted, it keeps its space.
rules.block: Applied with `block` or `collapse`: takes the full width.

cssVariables.title: CSS variables
cssVariables.description: Duration, delay and easing are set as inline styles from the props, so regular CSS doesn't override them.

items.--gem-transition-duration: Duration of the current phase. Set by `duration`. Change it only through the prop: the component uses that value to know when the phase ends.
items.--gem-transition-easing: Easing. Set by `easing`. It can be overridden with an `!important` utility, like in the Tailwind example.
items.--gem-transition-offset: Slide distance. Defaults to `0.75rem` and can be changed with CSS.

types.title: Exported types
types.description: Available from @gem-org/gem-system to type your own wrappers.

presence.title: Presence
presence.description: When it shows and what happens on exit.

items.in: `true` makes the content enter and `false` makes it exit.
items.children: Content, or a function that receives the current status.
items.appear: Also animates the first mount when `in` is already `true`.
items.unmountOnExit: Unmounts the content once it finishes exiting. With `false` it stays in the DOM, transparent and inert, taking up space.
items.duration: Duration in milliseconds. `{ enter, exit }` splits the timing.
items.delay: Delay in milliseconds, on enter and exit.
items.block: Takes the full container width. `collapse` always does.
items.onEnter: Enter starts, with the initial state applied.
items.onEntered: Enter finished. Also runs on the first mount without `appear`.
items.style: Inline styles. Merged with the variables the component sets.
